metadata.title: Primary and Secondary Raynaud: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
top_takeaways: Raynaud phenomenon is classified into primary (PRP) and secondary (SRP) types, which differ in pathogenesis, severity, and potential for severe complications like tissue loss.
Management of Raynaud phenomenon incorporates both lifestyle modifications and pharmacologic therapies, with a critical focus on treating any underlying systemic conditions in SRP.
Advanced imaging modalities may facilitate earlier detection of SRP, while management for severe cases can include botulinum toxin therapy and surgical interventions.

recommendations.statement: Treating the underlying systemic condition is essential to improving vascular symptoms and preventing complications in patients with secondary Raynaud phenomenon (SRP).
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Treating the underlying systemic condition is essential to improving vascular symptoms and preventing complications in patients with secondary Raynaud

recommendations.statement: Botulinum toxin therapy and surgical intervention may be considered for severe cases of Raynaud phenomenon refractory to conventional therapies.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with severe Raynaud phenomenon and impending tissue loss or ischemia
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Botulinum toxin therapy and surgical intervention may be considered for severe cases of Raynaud phenomenon refractory to conventional therapies.
